account:
Something more than an ordinary lighting inspection seems to be planned for eighteen in the great hall. The secretary recorded it as an approved inspection while preserving my usual appointments, but builder has asked that the hall stay closed until then. Builder also asked neighbour to escort me inside for a 'service acknowledgement.' Neighbour knows about that request but leaves the details to the organisers, despite my questions about whose service is being recognised.

There is also a community supper. Neighbour has been asking people for spare bread or grain, and builder said innkeeper coordinates hospitality. I heard townsfolk report innkeeper carrying a sack of bread to the town hall. Now builder, innkeeper and freight are all waiting near the hall; baker is nearby. Secretary says they will accompany me at eighteen, and neighbour appears to have followed me back after tea. My attempts to question innkeeper mostly produced replies I could not hear, so I do not know their explanation.

My suspicion is that the inspection is a pretext for a surprise gathering, perhaps an acknowledgement of my own service with a communal meal. That is not confirmed: nobody has identified the honouree or explicitly explained the connection between supper and inspection. The preparations look cooperative rather than threatening. I have kept today's appointments and have now returned for the sixteen-thirty office appointment; I intend to respect the closed hall and attend at eighteen.
